title: House band at the Eagles Ballroom in Milwaukee
summary: In high school he played tenor and clarinet in the ballroom house band five nights a week, meeting visiting bands like Paul Whiteman's.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Did any of these groups come by your home town, early on?

Later, but by that time I was in high school and I was now in the house band at the Eagles Ballroom. And we had many bands coming in across the country to play opposite, including Paul Whiteman. So I got to meet a lot of these people whom I had been hearing only on records and on the radio, and getting to meet them. And these were important times for me, very important.
This house band, was it something that was weekly, or every --
No, it was five nights a week and we had one matinee.
Is that right? What kind of shows?

Well, it was a ballroom. It was for dancing and they had two big bands, the house band and a travelling band in constantly. And all the hit bands, people like Coon- Saunders and Austin Wiley would come in from Cleveland. So I got to hear a lot of players that I ordinarily would not have heard.
It was a great kind of ground to lay the groundwork with.
What was the makeup of this house band instrumentally?

As I remember, we had about four brass, three or four. I think, two trumpets, two trombones, sometimes maybe three trumpets if you were lucky. And maybe three saxophones, two altos and a tenor. And if there were four, sometimes a baritone.
And you were playing saxophone and clarinet?
I was playing tenor and clarinet at that point.
